#### Step 4.6 — `cartDrawerContainer.tsx`: the real assembly (inserted 2026-09-20, built after 5.1 — see note)

**Numbering note.** Labeled 4.6 because it's the piece B4 was always missing, not because it builds before B5's step 5.1 — it doesn't. It builds **last** among every B4/B5 content piece, because it needs all of them finished first: `cartItemMapper` (3.4), `useCartMergeAndCap` (4.2), `useCartMessages` (4.3), `ZimmCartItemActions` (4.4), `ZimmCartEmptyState` (4.5), and `ZimmCartButtonGroup` (5.1). Commit order (below) reflects this; the step numbering doesn't need to.

**Why this step exists.** Found during step 4.2's own scoping (2026-09-19/20): `ZimmCartDrawer` (built commit 6) takes `children` as a prop and says so in its own docblock — *"the caller supplies the list... wired in a later commit in this same plan"* — but no step anywhere ever claimed that later commit. Same root cause as step 3.5's own insertion: a component built and tested in isolation, with its real integration point described in prose but never turned into an actual manifest line. `useCartMergeAndCap`'s own second call site (the "render guard," per its own step 4.2 text) has the same problem — no file was ever named for it. Both gaps share one fix: this container is the file that was missing.

**Changes.** New file `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (+ `.test.tsx`) — already in B4's manifest (Tier 3, `@pwa-squad-a`), just never claimed by a step. Modifies nothing else — `ProductItem` already has the `secondaryActions` prop slot built and wired (confirmed: `product-item/index.tsx:176,257,365`), so this step only fills it, it doesn't add it.

This container is the thing that:
1. Owns `useCurrentBasket()` — the one thing `components.md` forbids under `overrides/app/components/`, which is exactly why this lives under `overrides/app/pages/cart/` instead (open question 8's own resolution, finally acted on).
2. Maps each basket line through `cartItemMapper.ts` into `ProductItem` props, rendering the result as `ZimmCartDrawer`'s `children`.
3. Calls `useCartMergeAndCap` as the render guard on every render — the second of its two call sites; the first (the post-auth callback) was already wired into `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` back in step 4.2 itself.
4. Supplies each item's `secondaryActions` with a real `ZimmCartItemActions`, wired to the actual remove/wishlist-move mutations — not a placeholder.
5. Emits through `useCartMessages` wherever a message is actually needed, passing the result into `ZimmCartDrawer`'s `messages` slot.
6. Renders `ZimmCartEmptyState` in place of `children` when the basket has zero items.
7. Renders `ZimmCartButtonGroup` as `ZimmCartDrawer`'s `footer` slot.
8. Does **not** own `isOpen`/`onClose` itself — those arrive as props from whatever mounts this container (the final step, §9, via its own `useCartDrawer()` provider). This container's job is basket *content*, not the drawer's open/closed lifecycle — confirmed against `ZimmCartDrawer`'s own existing, unchanged prop contract (`isOpen`/`onClose` already required, already built).

**Also corrects §9's own text (see "B1 — revised file manifest" below):** that section currently says to mount `<ZimmCartDrawer />` directly in `_app`. Once this container exists, `_app` should mount `<CartDrawerContainer />` instead, which renders `<ZimmCartDrawer>` internally — otherwise the app repeats the exact gap already found in the base "AddToCartModal" precedent that section cites: `AddToCartModalProvider` is mounted in base `_app` today, but `<AddToCartModal />` itself is never rendered anywhere, base or override (confirmed by grepping the entire `retail-react-app` package) — so add-to-cart already shows no visual feedback in this app, and "mirroring" that pattern literally would just build the cart drawer the same non-functional way.

**Pass criteria.**
1. Renders one `ProductItem` per real basket line, using `cartItemMapper.ts`'s output verbatim — not a second, hand-rolled mapping.
2. `useCartMergeAndCap`'s render guard actually runs on a basket-driven re-render, and is proven (not assumed) to no-op while `useIsMutating()` is non-zero — this proves the wiring, step 4.2's own criterion 2 already proved the function. **Clarified 2026-09-20 (flagged by step 4.2's own Implementer, not yet a bug since this step hasn't been built):** "runs on a re-render" does not mean calling `capBasketQuantities` bare in the component's render body — that fires a side-effecting async function (it can issue a real mutation) during render, which React does not guarantee runs once, in order, or at all, and is a real correctness/purity violation, not just a style nit. Call it from `useEffect(() => { capBasketQuantities(basket); }, [basket])`, keyed on the basket state that actually changed — "runs on a basket-driven re-render" describes *when* the guard should trigger (whenever the basket's own relevant state changes), not *where in the render cycle* to place the call.
3. Each rendered item's `secondaryActions` is a real, wired `ZimmCartItemActions` — not a placeholder or omitted prop.
4. Empty basket renders `ZimmCartEmptyState`, not an empty `children` array.
5. `footer` slot renders `ZimmCartButtonGroup`; `messages` slot renders whatever `useCartMessages` currently holds.
6. This container receives `isOpen`/`onClose` as props and does not read or own drawer-open state itself.
7. `grep -rn "<ZimmCartDrawer" overrides/app` returns exactly one production call site: this container (plus its own stories/tests).

**Loop.** Full — this is a first-time, multi-piece wiring step exactly like 3.5's insertion was, and a mistake here is exactly as invisible to any single piece's own per-file review as that one was.

---

## 5. Loop configuration

## 5.0 Verification standard (added 2026-09-19, applies to every remaining step, 3.6 onward)

Six real, currently-shipped defects were found in commits already scored PASS on Design fidelity,
by a from-scratch re-audit that rendered the real components live instead of reading source and
Figma side by side. Every one of the six traces back to one of the gaps below. These are now
mandatory for every remaining step's Design-fidelity check — not optional rigor, a gate. When
dispatching Tester/Scorer for 3.6 onward, brief them with this section explicitly: they start
each run with no memory of today, so the standard has to be restated, not assumed carried over.

1. **A rendered-output claim needs a live measurement citation, not a source read.** "The recipe
   sets `fontWeight: 500`" is not the same claim as "the rendered text measures `font-weight: 500`
   in a real browser" — the first can be true while the second is false. Every Design-fidelity
   PASS from here on cites an actual measured value (computed style, bounding box, or a real
   screenshot) against the actual Figma-sourced value, for every property being signed off, not
   just the ones that seem most at-risk.
2. **A wrapper's correct style does not prove a nested element inherits it.** Two of the six
   defects were exactly this shape: `textStyle`/`fontWeight` correctly set on a container, silently
   lost before reaching the actual visible text, because the nested element was either a Chakra
   component with its own competing theme registration (`Heading`, and by extension `Button`/
   `IconButton`/`Modal`/anything imported from `@chakra-ui/react` un-wrapped in a plain `chakra.*`
   factory) or a literal HTML tag with its own default rendering (`<b>`, via a base SFCC
   component). Whenever a style is applied above a boundary like that, verify the leaf text node's
   own computed style directly — inheritance is not something to assume across it.
3. **A previously-recorded "confirmed correct" is not permanent proof.** This exact document's own
   audit trail (`figma-reference/discrepancies.md`) both found real bugs *and*, twice, had to
   retract its own "confirmed" claims once they were checked against a real render instead of
   restated from a prior pass. Re-verify against a live render before citing an earlier pass as
   settled, especially for anything touching the same file again.
4. **Storybook `play` functions auto-run on load.** A live check against a story with a `play`
   function is measuring the *post-play* state by the time any normal wait resolves, not the
   initial seed — sample within ~100ms of mount if the true initial state matters, and never treat
   a play function's own scripted end-state as a seeding bug.
5. **Read the real, current JSX before asserting how two elements relate.** More than one
   mis-scoped finding this pass came from reasoning about layout from a written description
   instead of the actual current source — siblings vs. nested, same container vs. different, is
   checkable in seconds and shouldn't be inferred.
6. **A fix for one interaction can silently break a different one.** The focus-ring fix's first
   attempt passed its own new test and broke backdrop-click-to-close, undetected until the full
   existing suite was re-run. Any interaction/focus/event-handling change re-runs the component's
   *entire* existing test suite, not just the new assertion, before being called done.
7. **Mutation-test every new test, and disclose when jsdom genuinely can't.** Revert the fix,
   confirm the new test fails with the real wrong value; restore, confirm it passes. If a property
   (native `:focus-visible` matching is the known example so far) can't be made mutation-sensitive
   under jsdom, say so directly in the test's own comment rather than claim proof the test doesn't
   actually provide — the real proof in that case is the live-browser verification, cited as such.
8. **No AI attribution, no third-person references to any person, in any commit message.**
   Objective and technical only — what changed and why, not who caught it or confirmed it. Two
   rounds of whole-branch correction this pass were both this exact category.

## 6. Open questions

These block the handoff. None is a decision I should make for you.

1. **`.github/workflows/qa.yml` is Tier 1 and owner approval is not confirmed.** B0 is BLOCKED until either the authenticated `gh` login is verified in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` or a named approving review is secured. Until B0 lands, every cart PR gets `e2e_scope: skip` and no PR-time E2E.

2. **`overrides/app/components/item-variant/` has no CODEOWNERS entry and there is no catch-all.** Five files with an 11-surface blast radius would merge with **no required reviewer**. Adding the entry is a Tier 1 Governance change to `CODEOWNERS`, explicitly outside my scope. Your call: add it as a separate ticket first, or accept that the widest-reaching part of this change is ungoverned and compensate with a manually-requested reviewer on B2.

3. **`overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` is also ungoverned, and the merge call changes auth behaviour for three surfaces outside the cart** (`header/rightBar`, `drawer-menu`, `product-view`). Not in `frozenFiles.md`, not in `protectedFiles.md`'s shared-hooks list, no CODEOWNERS entry. This is a second instance of #2 and arguably the more dangerous one. Does B4 need an explicitly requested reviewer, and does the cross-surface behaviour change need Hard Rule #10 scope confirmation from you before it is written?

4. **`overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` does not exist.** The settled decision says "use `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts`, not the base hook" — but that file is absent, and the path is listed in `protectedFiles.md` and routed in CODEOWNERS to `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. So honouring the decision literally means **creating a Tier 2 shared hook** this bundle has not budgeted a review for. My recommendation: import the base hook at `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast` and wrap it in our own untiered `useCartMessages.ts`. That satisfies the decision's actual intent (one handler, SFCC-404 is a one-file swap), costs no Tier 2 review, and automatically picks up the override the day someone creates it. I have **not** applied this — the decision is yours to confirm.

5. **The stepper's `+` and `−` are a mismatched pair.** `MinusIcon` is a Zimmermann/Figma icon in `overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx`; `PlusIcon` is re-exported from the base template in `index.tsx`. That file's own comments show the established pattern of migrating an icon into `zimm.tsx` when the base glyph is wrong (`CloseIcon`: "off-centre glyph within its viewBox"; the chevrons: filled vs stroked). AGENTS.md is explicit: if a required icon is missing from the overrides set, **ask — do not substitute a visually different one**. Is the base `PlusIcon` acceptable against Figma's `Icon_plus`, or does it need adding to `zimm.tsx`?

6. **Apple Pay and Google Pay marks do not exist.** `zimm.tsx` has `ZimmAppleSignInIcon` and `ZimmGoogleSignInIcon` — sign-in marks, not Pay marks — and there is no `applePay`/`googlePay` asset anywhere in `overrides/app`. Both are brand-licensed artwork with usage rules. SFCC-275 AC1 requires 48×24 logos. Same AGENTS.md rule applies: ask, do not substitute. This is the only part of B5 that cannot pass.

import React from 'react'
import {
    Alert,
    AlertIcon,
    AlertTitle,
    CloseButton,
    Spacer,
    useToast as useChakraToast
} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui'

/**
 * Display a toast message on the screen.
 * This is a custom hook to handle showing toasts in the app, preventing duplicate toasts and to add action elements
 * to toasts when required. It supports all props supported by Chakra toast.
 *
 * @param {string} title Message text to be displayed in toast
 * @param {string} id - id provided to the toast to avoid duplicate toast ids, use it if multiple toasts are needed
 * @param {string} status Semantic state of the toast - success | error | info | warning
 * @param {node} action Optional component to be displayed in the toast (eg. Button to allow user to perform action)
 * @param {string} position The placement of the toast on screen
 * @param {number} duration The delay before the toast hides (in milliseconds)
 */
export function useToast() {
    const toast = useChakraToast()

    return ({
        title,
        description,
        status,
        action,
        position = 'top-right',
        duration = 5000,
        variant = 'subtle',
        isClosable = true
    }) => {
        let toastConfig = {
            title,
            description,
            status,
            isClosable,
            position,
            duration,
            variant
        }

        if (action) {
            toastConfig = {
                ...toastConfig,

                render: ({onClose}) => (
                    <Alert status={status} variant="subtle" borderRadius="md" py={3} width="sm">
                        <AlertIcon />
                        <AlertTitle> {title} </AlertTitle>
                        <Spacer />
                        {action}
                        <Spacer />
                        <CloseButton onClick={onClose} />
                    </Alert>
                )
            }
        }
        toast(toastConfig)
    }
}

                render: ({onClose}) => (
                    <Alert status={status} variant="subtle" borderRadius="md" py={3} width="sm">
                        <AlertIcon />
                        <AlertTitle> {title} </AlertTitle>
                        <Spacer />
                        {action}
                        <Spacer />
                        <CloseButton onClick={onClose} />
                    </Alert>
                )
            }
        }
        toast(toastConfig)
    }
}

1	import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
2	import type { ShopperBasketsV2Types } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
3	import { useShopperBasketsV2Mutation as useShopperBasketsMutation } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
4	import { getMaxOrderQuantity } from 'app/utils/maxOrderQuantity';
5	
6	/**
7	 * The minimal basket shape this hook needs, regardless of which caller supplies it: the
8	 * post-auth callback (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`, wired in this step) passes the resolved value
9	 * of its own `mergeBasket` mutation directly; the cart drawer's render guard
10	 * (`overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx`, step 4.6 — not yet built) will pass its
11	 * own `useCurrentBasket()` data. `Pick`-narrowed, matching `cartItemMapper.ts`'s own established
12	 * pattern for taking an untyped-at-the-edges SDK response and narrowing it to only the fields a
13	 * pure function actually reads, rather than depending on the exact generic SDK response type
14	 * either caller's own mutation/query hook happens to produce.
15	 */
16	export type CartCapBasket = Pick<ShopperBasketsV2Types.Basket, 'basketId' | 'lastModified' | 'productItems'>;
17	
18	/**
19	 * Outcome of one `capBasketQuantities` call. A discriminated union (typescript.md's guidance for
20	 * variant/state modelling) rather than a boolean-plus-optional-error: each branch is something a
21	 * caller could reasonably want to react to differently, and no AC or copy exists yet for any of
22	 * them (that is `useCartMessages`, step 4.3, not built) — this file only reports what happened,
23	 * it does not decide what the shopper sees.
24	 */
25	export type CartCapResult =
26	  | { status: 'not-needed' }
27	  | { status: 'skipped'; reason: 'mutation-in-flight' | 'already-attempted-this-version' }
28	  | { status: 'corrected' }
29	  | { status: 'error'; error: unknown };
30	
31	/**
32	 * `getMaxOrderQuantity` is typed for a SCAPI product response (`id: string` required — see
33	 * `overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts`). A basket line item has no `id` field at all: only
34	 * `itemId`/`productId` (confirmed against the generated `BasketProductItem` type — verified via
35	 * a throwaway `tsc` repro that assigning a same-shaped object to a type requiring `id` fails
36	 * with "Property 'id' is missing"), so passing one directly does not type-check, despite it
37	 * carrying the same `{[key: string]: any}` catch-all a real `c_maxOrderQuantity` value would
38	 * arrive through once SFCC-268 ships. `product-item/index.tsx` already lives with the identical
39	 * gap at its own `getMaxOrderQuantity(product)` call site (`type SfccProduct = any`, lines 171
40	 * and 331) — narrowed here with an explicit, commented cast instead of a bare `any` parameter,
41	 * per typescript.md's "no `any` without an inline comment" rule.
42	 */
43	const getLineMaxOrderQuantity = (item: ShopperBasketsV2Types.BasketProductItem): number =>
44	  getMaxOrderQuantity(item as unknown as Parameters<typeof getMaxOrderQuantity>[0]);
45	
46	/**
47	 * A line needs correction once its quantity exceeds the cap — i.e. once it reaches the smallest
48	 * over-cap value (`max + 1`; `4` when `max` is `3`) or anything above it. Written as `quantity >
49	 * max` rather than comparing against a separately-named `max + 1` boundary, but the two are the
50	 * same comparison: this must be a "the whole range above the boundary" check, not an
51	 * exact-equality check against a single value — an equality check against `max + 1` alone would
52	 * correctly catch a line at 4 but wrongly leave a line at 5 or more uncorrected, which is
53	 * observably wrong against this hook's own test fixture (a line at 5 must reduce to 3, not stay
54	 * at 5).
55	 */
56	const needsQuantityCorrection = (
57	  item: ShopperBasketsV2Types.BasketProductItem,
58	): item is ShopperBasketsV2Types.BasketProductItem & { quantity: number } =>
59	  typeof item.quantity === 'number' && item.quantity > getLineMaxOrderQuantity(item);
60	
61	/**
62	 * SFCC baskets carry no explicit version counter. `basketId` + `lastModified` change together on
63	 * every write SFCC accepts (both real fields on the generated `Basket` type), so the pair is a
64	 * workable proxy for "the exact basket state a correction was last attempted against" — this is
65	 * this file's own reasoned choice, not sourced from an existing codebase precedent or doc.
66	 */
67	const getBasketVersionKey = (basket: CartCapBasket): string => `${basket.basketId ?? ''}:${basket.lastModified ?? ''}`;
68	
69	/**
70	 * Storage key for "which basket version has a correction already been attempted against."
71	 * Deliberately not a `useRef` — the post-auth callback (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`) and the
72	 * future render guard (step 4.6) each get their own separate `useCartMergeAndCap()` call, and
73	 * therefore their own separate refs, since they mount in two different React component trees. A
74	 * plain ref cannot coordinate between them. Piggybacking on the already-global `QueryClient` (the
75	 * same one `capBasketQuantities`'s own mutation-in-flight guard reads from — see that function's
76	 * own comment) via `getQueryData`/`setQueryData` gives real cross-instance-shared storage without
77	 * inventing a new module-level singleton or Context provider. It is also, unlike a React-render-
78	 * time hook value, live/imperative — reading and then
79	 * immediately writing it inside `capBasketQuantities` with no `await` in between (see that
80	 * function) leaves no window for two near-simultaneous calls to both pass the check before either
81	 * has recorded its attempt, since JavaScript runs that synchronous read-then-write as one
82	 * uninterruptible step.
83	 */
84	const CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY = ['zimmCartMergeAndCap', 'attemptedBasketVersion'] as const;
85	
86	export type UseCartMergeAndCapReturn = {
87	  /**
88	   * Checks every basket line against `getMaxOrderQuantity` and, if any line exceeds its cap,
89	   * issues one `updateItemsInBasket` write reducing every over-cap line to its own max in a
90	   * single request (matching the SFCC-11 plan's "one write" framing even when more than one line
91	   * needs correcting). Resolves only once that write — if one was issued — has fully settled, so
92	   * a caller sequencing merge -> cap -> a future wishlist-resume can `await` this in turn without
93	   * racing it.
94	   */
95	  capBasketQuantities: (basket: CartCapBasket) => Promise<CartCapResult>;
96	};
97	
98	/**
99	 * Hook — the shared "cap" half of SFCC-250's merge-then-cap flow. Two callers share this one
100	 * implementation, not two copies: the post-auth callback inside `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own
101	 * `isRegistered` effect (wired in this step, right after that effect's existing `mergeBasket`
102	 * call), and the cart drawer's render guard, which will live in
103	 * `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (not yet built — a later step, 4.6, wires
104	 * that second call site; this hook is written to support it, not to assume it already exists).
105	 *
106	 * Per rules-of-hooks, call this at the top level of whichever hook or component needs it — never
107	 * from inside a `useEffect` callback — and invoke the returned `capBasketQuantities` function
108	 * itself from inside the effect/render path instead.
109	 *
110	 * @returns `capBasketQuantities`, the one function both callers invoke.
111	 */
112	export const useCartMergeAndCap = (): UseCartMergeAndCapReturn => {
113	  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
114	  const updateItemsInBasket = useShopperBasketsMutation('updateItemsInBasket');
115	
116	  const capBasketQuantities = async (basket: CartCapBasket): Promise<CartCapResult> => {
117	    // No-op while any mutation is in flight (this hook's own prior correction, the merge that
118	    // just ran, a shopper's manual quantity edit — anything) so this can never race a write
119	    // already under way. See this function's own JSDoc.
120	    //
121	    // REWORK (round 1, Tester-confirmed defect): this must be a LIVE read taken at the moment
122	    // this function actually runs — not a React-render-time value closed over at this hook's own
123	    // top level. `capBasketQuantities` is captured once by its caller and invoked later, from
124	    // inside an async callback (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s `mergeBasket.mutate(...).onSuccess`,
125	    // itself only reachable after a real network round trip) with no guarantee that hook instance
126	    // re-renders in between. A `useIsMutating()` value read at this hook's own top level (the
127	    // original approach here) would still reflect whatever mutation count existed at that earlier
128	    // render, not the real state at the moment this guard actually needs to check it.
129	    //
130	    // `queryClient.isMutating(filters?)` (confirmed against the installed
131	    // `@tanstack/query-core@4.43.0` source — a single deduped version across this project's whole
132	    // dependency tree, per `npm ls @tanstack/react-query` — `node_modules/@tanstack/query-core/
133	    // build/lib/queryClient.esm.js`: `isMutating(filters) { return this.mutationCache.findAll(
134	    // {...filters, fetching: true}).length; }`) computes this fresh from the live mutation cache
135	    // on every call. It is the exact same computation `useIsMutating()` itself wraps in
136	    // `useSyncExternalStore` for React reactivity (`node_modules/@tanstack/react-query/build/lib/
137	    // useIsMutating.esm.js`: `() => queryClient.isMutating(filters)`), just read directly instead
138	    // of through a render-synced subscription — so this preserves the exact same "every mutation
139	    // anywhere in the app" scope this guard has always had (commerce-sdk-react's basket mutation
140	    // hooks set no `mutationKey`, so an unscoped call is still the only reading that sees all of
141	    // them), it now just reads that scope live instead of stale.
142	    if (queryClient.isMutating() > 0) {
143	      return { status: 'skipped', reason: 'mutation-in-flight' };
144	    }
145	
146	    const correctedItems = (basket.productItems ?? []).filter(needsQuantityCorrection).map((item) => ({
147	      itemId: item.itemId,
148	      productId: item.productId,
149	      quantity: getLineMaxOrderQuantity(item),
150	    }));
151	
152	    if (correctedItems.length === 0) {
153	      return { status: 'not-needed' };
154	    }
155	
156	    if (!basket.basketId) {
157	      // No basketId means there is nothing valid to address a write at — surface this as an
158	      // error rather than silently doing nothing, so a caller can tell "nothing needed fixing"
159	      // apart from "something needed fixing and couldn't be".
160	      return { status: 'error', error: new Error('useCartMergeAndCap: basket is missing a basketId.') };
161	    }
162	
163	    const versionKey = getBasketVersionKey(basket);
164	    if (queryClient.getQueryData<string>(CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY) === versionKey) {
165	      // Loop guard: a correction has already been attempted against this exact basket state,
166	      // whether it succeeded or failed — do not retry it. See CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY's own
167	      // comment for why this is a live cache read rather than a per-instance ref, and why
168	      // setting it below, before the `await`, is what keeps this race-free.
169	      return { status: 'skipped', reason: 'already-attempted-this-version' };
170	    }
171	    queryClient.setQueryData(CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY, versionKey);
172	
173	    try {
174	      await updateItemsInBasket.mutateAsync({
175	        parameters: { basketId: basket.basketId },
176	        body: correctedItems,
177	      });
178	      return { status: 'corrected' };
179	    } catch (error) {
180	      // Surfaced to the caller, not retried: the version is already marked attempted above, so a
181	      // later call against this same unchanged basket state returns 'skipped' rather than
182	      // hammering the server again — no retry storm.
183	      return { status: 'error', error };
184	    }
185	  };
186	
187	  return { capBasketQuantities };
188	};

1	import React from 'react';
2	import type { Preview, Decorator } from '@storybook/react-webpack5';
3	import { ChakraProvider } from '@chakra-ui/react';
4	import { IntlProvider } from 'react-intl';
5	import theme from '../overrides/app/theme';
6	import { ZimmTokensGlobal } from '../overrides/app/theme/zimmTokensGlobal';
7	import { ZimmFontFace } from '../overrides/app/theme/fontFace';
8	import { CHAKRA_TOAST_A11Y_EXCLUDE } from './a11yExcludes';
9	
10	// @salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime's browser-side getConfig() (utils/ssr-config.client.js) just
11	// reads window.__CONFIG__, which the real app's SSR bootstrap script sets and Storybook never
12	// does — every call site that reads getConfig().app (Zimmermann's own, e.g.
13	// overrides/app/config/contentful.ts, and base SFCC vendor code, e.g. use-auth-modal.js's and
14	// otp-auth/index.jsx's getConfig().app.login) throws in Storybook without this. `login: {}` is
15	// needed alongside `app: {}` — every other getConfig().app.* read in base SFCC guards with `?.`
16	// or `|| {}`, but otp-auth/index.jsx's `const {tokenLength} = getConfig().app.login` does not,
17	// so `.login` itself must already be an object. `sites` is needed for any story whose play
18	// function clicks a button that calls useNavigation() → removeSiteLocaleFromPath() →
19	// getConfigMatcher() → getSites(), which throws when sites is empty. Not a copy of real config
20	// values — just enough shape for vendor code's unguarded reads.
21	if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
22	  (window as typeof window & { __CONFIG__?: { app: Record<string, unknown> } }).__CONFIG__ = {
23	    app: {
24	      login: {},
25	      sites: [
26	        {
27	          id: 'ZimmermannAU',
28	          alias: 'au',
29	          l10n: {supportedLocales: [{id: 'en-AU', alias: 'en-AU'}]},
30	        },
31	      ],
32	    },
33	  };
34	}
35	
36	// ZimmTokensGlobal injects the --zimm-* :root custom properties, mirroring what
37	// _app-config does in the app. Without it, the .zimm-* global classes and the
38	// var(--zimm-*) component overrides (button/header/listMenu) render unresolved in
39	// Storybook. Same shared source as the app, so the two cannot drift.
40	//
41	// ZimmFontFace declares the self-hosted Futura Round faces, likewise mirroring
42	// _app-config. Without it Storybook renders the fallback stack while the app renders
43	// Futura Round — the fallback measures ~13% wider, so any visual comparison made in
44	// Storybook would not match the app or Figma. Font files are served here by the
45	// staticDirs mapping in .storybook/main.js.
46	const withChakra: Decorator = (Story) => (
47	  <ChakraProvider theme={theme}>
48	    <ZimmFontFace />
49	    <ZimmTokensGlobal />
50	    <Story />
51	  </ChakraProvider>
52	);
53	
54	const withIntl: Decorator = (Story) => (
55	  <IntlProvider locale="en-AU" defaultLocale="en-AU">
56	    <Story />
57	  </IntlProvider>
58	);
59	
60	const preview: Preview = {
61	  parameters: {
62	    controls: {
63	      matchers: {
64	        color: /(background|color)$/i,
65	        date: /date$/i,
66	      },
67	    },
68	    layout: 'centered',
69	    a11y: {
70	      // 'error' causes a11y violations to fail test-storybook --ci runs
71	      test: 'error',
72	      // See a11yExcludes.ts — Storybook's parameters merge is shallow, so a story that sets
73	      // its own parameters.a11y.context.exclude REPLACES this array rather than extending it;
74	      // that file's own comment documents how a story adds to it instead.
75	      context: {
76	        exclude: CHAKRA_TOAST_A11Y_EXCLUDE,
77	      },
78	    },
79	  },
80	  decorators: [withChakra, withIntl],
81	};
82	
83	export default preview;

import React from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { ZimmIcon } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon';

const ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE = 'ZimmInlineMessage';

export type ZimmInlineMessageProps = {
  /**
   * Colour/severity only — this atom never decides which one applies. A caller may legitimately
   * pass `variant="warning"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word "error" (the cart
   * max-quantity message is exactly this case) — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for
   * why that's a deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation, not a mismatch to fix here.
   *
   * `success` added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull, 2026-09-18) for
   * the cart-line discount label ("20% off applied") — see this component's own docblock below.
   */
  variant: 'error' | 'warning' | 'success';
  /**
   * Message copy, rendered verbatim. This atom never derives, hardcodes, or paraphrases copy — a
   * caller supplies the already-resolved string (e.g. "This item is unavailable", "Quantity
   * unavailable in this size", "Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size" — SFCC-795
   * §11.2 exact copy).
   */
  text: string;
  /**
   * Overrides the root element's `data-testid`, defaulting to the pre-existing hardcoded
   * `'zimm-inline-message'` — every caller that omits this keeps that exact default, unchanged.
   * Added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3: a single cart line can now render both a discount label
   * (`variant="success"`) and an error/warning `message` at once (product-item/index.tsx), so two
   * `ZimmInlineMessage` instances can appear on one line — without a distinct testid per instance,
   * `getByTestId('zimm-inline-message')` would match both and throw.
   */
  dataTestId?: string;
  /**
   * SFCC-795 plan step 3.6 (accessibility sweep): stable id for a caller to reference via
   * `aria-describedby` on the control this message is actually about — the same
   * id-on-the-message + `aria-describedby`-on-the-control pairing `zimmTextInput/index.tsx`
   * already uses for its own helper/error text (`helperId`/`errorId`). Undefined (every existing
   * caller today) omits the `id` attribute entirely, unchanged from before this prop existed.
   *
   * Consumed by `product-item/index.tsx`: this message's one real-world consumer is
   * `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s two `ZimmButton variant="icon"` controls, so the id is forwarded as
   * `aria-describedby` on both of those buttons, not on a wrapping element — ARIA description is
   * computed per focused node, not inherited from an ancestor, so a screen-reader user tabbing to
   * either button would not hear a description set only on a container (confirmed against
   * `zimmDropdown/index.tsx`'s own precedent, which sets `aria-describedby` directly on its native
   * `chakra.button` trigger for the same reason). Getting `aria-describedby` onto the icon variant
   * at all required a small, additive addition to `ZimmButton` itself (`ariaDescribedBy` on
   * `ZimmIconButtonProps`, `zimmButton/index.tsx`) — `ZimmLabelButtonProps` already had the
   * equivalent prop, `ZimmIconButtonProps` did not.
   */
  id?: string;
};

/**
 * Atom — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2). Presentation only:
 * renders whatever `variant`/`text` it is given and never determines availability itself.
 * OOS/partial-OOS detection is SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's — both
 * later-sprint tickets this component does not, and should not, anticipate. No low-stock variant
 * exists in `ZimmInlineMessageProps['variant']` — a separate requirement explicitly forbids
 * low-stock messaging at the cart level (see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts).
 *
 * `aria-live="polite"` matches the same treatment this codebase already gives another transient,
 * non-input cart-line status value — ZimmQuantityStepper's own quantity display (its `value`
 * part, zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx) carries the identical `aria-live="polite"` treatment — so
 * a shopper using assistive tech is told about a message that appears/changes after their own
 * action, without requiring focus to move to it.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework (Marcel's own visual checkpoint against the real Figma file): the `warning`
 * variant renders a leading `info-solid` icon, `error` never does — confirmed against 3 real
 * cart-item instances in Figma file QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs: the two error-copy states (FULLY OOS
 * node 9323-101979, PARTIAL OOS node 9323-98397) have no icon in their message sub-tree; the
 * warning-copy state's own "Cart Item" instance (9323:106685 — one of 5 per-item rows inside the
 * "WARNINGS SHOWN" frame's "Cart-item-group", not that frame's separate SFCC-404
 * "Cart-level-messages" sibling — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts for the full parent-chain
 * citation) does. The icon is `aria-hidden` — the
 * message's own text plus `aria-live` already carry the full meaning to assistive tech, so the
 * icon is a purely visual (sighted-only) reinforcement of a severity already conveyed by colour
 * and copy, not an independent piece of information.
 *

 * ships no TypeScript types — this subpath falls through `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`'s

 * assigning `any` to any narrower type with no check, so the real correctness proof is the test
 * file's own direct comparison against a real `getPriceData` call, not this annotation alone.

  /** `findLowestPrice()`'s own `minPrice` — never `product.price` directly. This is the field
   *  `productListCardMapper.ts` does not use for its own `currentPrice` (it reads the flat

   *  `tieredPrices` at all (there is then no maximum to compute). */

1	import { useToast } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast';
2	
3	/**
4	 * `@salesforce/retail-react-app` ships no TypeScript types (AGENTS.md's "Commerce SDK types not
5	 * importable" gotcha) — `use-toast.js` falls through `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`'s catch-all
6	 * `declare module '@salesforce/retail-react-app/*'` (a shorthand ambient module declaration that
7	 * types the whole module `any` — see that file's own comment, and
8	 * `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s identical narrow-local-type pattern for
9	 * another untyped base function), so the real `useToast()` return value is implicitly `any`.
10	 * Declared narrow here, covering only the two fields this file actually sends (`title`, `status`)
11	 * rather than the base hook's full options surface (`description`, `action`, `position`,
12	 * `duration`, `variant`, `isClosable`) — nothing in this file uses those, so typing them would be
13	 * speculative. `status`'s four values are copied verbatim from the base hook's real accepted set
14	 * (not narrowed to only `'success' | 'warning'`), so a later message that genuinely needs `'error'`
15	 * or `'info'` — SFCC-404's rework, or any message added after this step — is already covered
16	 * without a signature change here.
17	 *
18	 * This is a type annotation documenting an assumed shape, not a runtime guarantee — TypeScript
19	 * allows asserting `any` to any narrower type with no check. The real proof is this file's own
20	 * test, which asserts the exact object the mocked toast function is called with.
21	 */
22	type CartToastStatus = 'success' | 'error' | 'info' | 'warning';
23	type CartToastFn = (options: {title: string; status: CartToastStatus}) => void;
24	
25	/**
26	 * The three real cart messages this step ships, copy verbatim from Figma (SFCC-11 plan step 4.3)
27	 * — this file never derives or paraphrases copy, only interpolates a product name into the one
28	 * message that needs it. SFCC-272's own AC text describes a generic stacked wording ("Item added
29	 * to Wishlist") for when more than one item has been added — deliberately not built here: a toast
30	 * has no aggregation concept, so that copy is only reachable once SFCC-404 ships real message
31	 * stacking. Until then every add uses this product-named variant, one toast per add.
32	 */
33	const getAddedToWishlistMessage = (productName: string): string => `${productName} added to Wishlist`;
34	const ALREADY_IN_WISHLIST_MESSAGE = 'An item in your bag already exists in Wishlist';
35	const MAX_QUANTITY_REACHED_MESSAGE = 'An item in your bag has reached maximum quantity';
36	
37	export type UseCartMessagesReturn = {
38	  /**
39	   * SFCC-272 AC5 — a single product was moved from the cart to the wishlist. `productName` is
40	   * interpolated into the copy on every call — never hardcode a specific product's name at a call
41	   * site. `success` status.
42	   */
43	  notifyAddedToWishlist: (productName: string) => void;
44	  /**
45	   * SFCC-272 AC6 — the item already exists in the shopper's wishlist; the caller leaves the cart
46	   * line untouched. Verbatim copy, no interpolation. `warning` status — see
47	   * `notifyMaxQuantityReached`'s own doc for why cart feedback that doesn't block anything reads
48	   * as a warning in this build, not an error.
49	   */
50	  notifyAlreadyInWishlist: () => void;
51	  /**
52	   * CAI-017 / SFCC-250 — a cart line has reached its maximum orderable quantity (the line is
53	   * already capped by `useCartMergeAndCap` before this ever fires). `warning`, not `error`:
54	   * CAI-017's own requirement text says "an error message will be displayed", but the Figma
55	   * rendering uses the warning variant and SFCC-250 AC4 confirms this never blocks checkout — this
56	   * build's own gate resolved the wording as meaning user-facing feedback, not literally Chakra's
57	   * error severity (the same reconciliation `ZimmInlineMessage`'s own `variant` prop documents —
58	   * `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage/index.tsx`: "a caller may
59	   * legitimately pass `variant=\"warning\"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word
60	   * `error`").
61	   */
62	  notifyMaxQuantityReached: () => void;
63	};
64	
65	/**
66	 * Hook — the one surface every cart toast message (success and warning today; whatever SFCC-404's
67	 * real stacking/aggregation rework needs later, including a genuine error) is sent through.
68	 * `emitCartMessage` below is the single call to the underlying toast function — a future rework
69	 * swaps what happens inside this one file, not a hunt across the cart UI for every place that
70	 * fires a toast.
71	 *
72	 * Wraps the **base** `useToast` (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast`) rather than a
73	 * new `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` — that path does not exist, and creating it would be an
74	 * unbudgeted Tier 2 change (`protectedFiles.md` would route it to both squads plus tier-2/tier-1
75	 * approvers). See the SFCC-11 plan's own resolved open question 4. This hook is the real "one
76	 * handler" the plan asks for; the base hook underneath it is just the interim renderer SFCC-404
77	 * replaces.
78	 *
79	 * @returns the three named cart-message senders callers actually invoke today. `emitCartMessage`
80	 * itself is intentionally not returned — nothing outside this file needs to send an
81	 * uncatalogued/arbitrary message yet, and a future message is one new named function here, not a
82	 * reason to widen this hook's public surface.
83	 */
84	export const useCartMessages = (): UseCartMessagesReturn => {
85	  // Real return type is implicit `any` (see CartToastFn's own docblock above) — asserted to the
86	  // local narrow type rather than left as `any`, so every call below is checked against the shape
87	  // this file actually depends on.
88	  const toast = useToast() as CartToastFn;
89	
90	  const emitCartMessage = (title: string, status: CartToastStatus): void => {
91	    // SFCC-404: this is the one real call to the underlying toast function. When SFCC-404's real
92	    // stacking/aggregation rework lands, this is the only line that changes.
93	    toast({title, status});
94	  };
95	
96	  return {
97	    notifyAddedToWishlist: (productName: string) =>
98	      emitCartMessage(getAddedToWishlistMessage(productName), 'success'),
99	    notifyAlreadyInWishlist: () => emitCartMessage(ALREADY_IN_WISHLIST_MESSAGE, 'warning'),
100	    notifyMaxQuantityReached: () => emitCartMessage(MAX_QUANTITY_REACHED_MESSAGE, 'warning'),
101	  };
102	};
103

1	import { useToast } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast';
2	
3	/**
4	 * `@salesforce/retail-react-app` ships no TypeScript types (AGENTS.md's "Commerce SDK types not
5	 * importable" gotcha) — `use-toast.js` falls through `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`'s catch-all
6	 * `declare module '@salesforce/retail-react-app/*'` (a shorthand ambient module declaration that
7	 * types the whole module `any` — see that file's own comment, and
8	 * `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s identical narrow-local-type pattern for
9	 * another untyped base function), so the real `useToast()` return value is implicitly `any`.
10	 * Declared narrow here, covering only the two fields this file actually sends (`title`, `status`)
11	 * rather than the base hook's full options surface (`description`, `action`, `position`,
12	 * `duration`, `variant`, `isClosable`) — nothing in this file uses those, so typing them would be
13	 * speculative. `status`'s four values are copied verbatim from the base hook's real accepted set
14	 * (not narrowed to only `'success' | 'warning'`), so a later message that genuinely needs `'error'`
15	 * or `'info'` — SFCC-404's rework, or any message added after this step — is already covered
16	 * without a signature change here.
17	 *
18	 * This is a type annotation documenting an assumed shape, not a runtime guarantee — TypeScript
19	 * allows asserting `any` to any narrower type with no check. The real proof is this file's own
20	 * test, which asserts the exact object the mocked toast function is called with.
21	 */
22	type CartToastStatus = 'success' | 'error' | 'info' | 'warning';
23	type CartToastFn = (options: { title: string; status: CartToastStatus }) => void;
24	
25	/**
26	 * The three real cart messages this step ships, copy verbatim from Figma (SFCC-11 plan step 4.3)
27	 * — this file never derives or paraphrases copy, only interpolates a product name into the one
28	 * message that needs it. SFCC-272's own AC text describes a generic stacked wording ("Item added
29	 * to Wishlist") for when more than one item has been added — deliberately not built here: a toast
30	 * has no aggregation concept, so that copy is only reachable once SFCC-404 ships real message
31	 * stacking. Until then every add uses this product-named variant, one toast per add.
32	 */
33	const getAddedToWishlistMessage = (productName: string): string => `${productName} added to Wishlist`;
34	const ALREADY_IN_WISHLIST_MESSAGE = 'An item in your bag already exists in Wishlist';
35	const MAX_QUANTITY_REACHED_MESSAGE = 'An item in your bag has reached maximum quantity';
36	
37	export type UseCartMessagesReturn = {
38	  /**
39	   * SFCC-272 AC5 — a single product was moved from the cart to the wishlist. `productName` is
40	   * interpolated into the copy on every call — never hardcode a specific product's name at a call
41	   * site. `success` status.
42	   */
43	  notifyAddedToWishlist: (productName: string) => void;
44	  /**
45	   * SFCC-272 AC6 — the item already exists in the shopper's wishlist; the caller leaves the cart
46	   * line untouched. Verbatim copy, no interpolation. `warning` status — see
47	   * `notifyMaxQuantityReached`'s own doc for why cart feedback that doesn't block anything reads
48	   * as a warning in this build, not an error.
49	   */
50	  notifyAlreadyInWishlist: () => void;
51	  /**
52	   * CAI-017 / SFCC-250 — a cart line has reached its maximum orderable quantity (the line is
53	   * already capped by `useCartMergeAndCap` before this ever fires). `warning`, not `error`:
54	   * CAI-017's own requirement text says "an error message will be displayed", but the Figma
55	   * rendering uses the warning variant and SFCC-250 AC4 confirms this never blocks checkout — this
56	   * build's own gate resolved the wording as meaning user-facing feedback, not literally Chakra's
57	   * error severity (the same reconciliation `ZimmInlineMessage`'s own `variant` prop documents —
58	   * `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage/index.tsx`: "a caller may
59	   * legitimately pass `variant=\"warning\"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word
60	   * `error`").
61	   */
62	  notifyMaxQuantityReached: () => void;
63	};
64	
65	/**
66	 * Hook — the one surface every cart toast message (success and warning today; whatever SFCC-404's
67	 * real stacking/aggregation rework needs later, including a genuine error) is sent through.
68	 * `emitCartMessage` below is the single call to the underlying toast function — a future rework
69	 * swaps what happens inside this one file, not a hunt across the cart UI for every place that
70	 * fires a toast.
71	 *
72	 * Wraps the **base** `useToast` (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast`) rather than a
73	 * new `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` — that path does not exist, and creating it would be an
74	 * unbudgeted Tier 2 change (`protectedFiles.md` would route it to both squads plus tier-2/tier-1
75	 * approvers). See the SFCC-11 plan's own resolved open question 4. This hook is the real "one
76	 * handler" the plan asks for; the base hook underneath it is just the interim renderer SFCC-404
77	 * replaces.
78	 *
79	 * @returns the three named cart-message senders callers actually invoke today. `emitCartMessage`
80	 * itself is intentionally not returned — nothing outside this file needs to send an
81	 * uncatalogued/arbitrary message yet, and a future message is one new named function here, not a
82	 * reason to widen this hook's public surface.
83	 */
84	export const useCartMessages = (): UseCartMessagesReturn => {
85	  // Real return type is implicit `any` (see CartToastFn's own docblock above) — asserted to the
86	  // local narrow type rather than left as `any`, so every call below is checked against the shape
87	  // this file actually depends on.
88	  const toast = useToast() as CartToastFn;
89	
90	  const emitCartMessage = (title: string, status: CartToastStatus): void => {
91	    // SFCC-404: this is the one real call to the underlying toast function. When SFCC-404's real
92	    // stacking/aggregation rework lands, this is the only line that changes.
93	    toast({ title, status });
94	  };
95	
96	  return {
97	    notifyAddedToWishlist: (productName: string) => emitCartMessage(getAddedToWishlistMessage(productName), 'success'),
98	    notifyAlreadyInWishlist: () => emitCartMessage(ALREADY_IN_WISHLIST_MESSAGE, 'warning'),
99	    notifyMaxQuantityReached: () => emitCartMessage(MAX_QUANTITY_REACHED_MESSAGE, 'warning'),
100	  };
101	};

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';

5	const ZIMM_CART_DRAWER_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartDrawer';
6	
7	// SFCC-315 builds the drawer shell only — SFCC-277/272 (later commits in this same 18-commit
8	// plan) will replace this with the real empty-bag component. This placeholder exists only so
9	// the body isn't blank/broken-looking in the meantime.
10	const EMPTY_BAG_PLACEHOLDER_TEXT = 'Your bag is empty.';
11	
12	export type ZimmCartDrawerProps = {
13	  /** Whether the drawer is open. */
14	  isOpen: boolean;
15	  /** Called on backdrop click, Escape, and the close button (all via ZimmDrawer/Chakra's Drawer). */
16	  onClose: () => void;
17	  /** Number of line items in the bag. Drives the header title ("BAG • {itemCount}" vs
18	   *  "YOUR BAG IS EMPTY") and whether `children` or the interim empty-state placeholder renders. */
19	  itemCount: number;
20	  /** Element to focus once the drawer finishes closing — see ZimmDrawer's own doc (AC10
21	   *  focus-return); without this Chakra falls back to focusing document.body. */
22	  finalFocusRef?: React.RefObject<HTMLElement>;
23	  /** Cart line items. This organism owns no item-rendering logic itself — the caller supplies
24	   *  the list (SFCC-270's ProductItem, wired in a later commit in this same plan). Rendered only
25	   *  while itemCount > 0. */
26	  children: React.ReactNode;
27	  /** Reserved slot for SFCC-404's message-aggregation system (validation/error/promo banners).
28	   *  Always rendered, even with nothing passed — see zimmCartDrawer.css.ts's `messages` part:
29	   *  the band reserves height regardless, so the drawer doesn't change position when a message
30	   *  appears or disappears. */
31	  messages?: React.ReactNode;
32	  /** Reserved slot for SFCC-275's button group (checkout / continue shopping). Not built in this
33	   *  commit (SFCC-315 is shell-only) — this organism only provides the slot it will render into
34	   *  later. */
35	  footer?: React.ReactNode;
36	};
37	
38	/**
39	 * SFCC-315 — the Cart drawer shell. Wraps ZimmDrawer (size="xLarge") with the cart-specific
40	 * header title, a height-reserving messages band, a responsive items/totals layout, and a
41	 * footer slot.
42	 *
43	 * Deliberately not wired to a trigger yet — no `_app`/`product-view` changes, no
44	 * `useCartDrawer` hook, no button-group content, no real empty-state body, no message
45	 * aggregation. All of those are separate, later commits in this same 18-commit plan — this
46	 * organism is exercised only via its own Storybook stories today.
47	 *
48	 * Figma-fidelity audit fix, 2026-09-19: `ZimmDrawer`'s `title` was passed with no `titleStyle`,
49	 * so it silently took that prop's default (`'large'` → `heading1`, 24px) instead of the Figma
50	 * spec for this header ("BAG • #", 14px medium — `body2Strong`). Measured live before the fix:
51	 * 24px/400/32px against the 14px/500 spec. `ZimmDrawer` itself already supports both correctly
52	 * (`titleStyle="small"` → `body2Strong`, confirmed against `typography.ts`) — this was a missing
53	 * prop at the call site, not a defect in `ZimmDrawer`.
54	 *
55	 * @param props see ZimmCartDrawerProps
56	 */
57	export const ZimmCartDrawer = ({
58	  isOpen,
59	  onClose,
60	  itemCount,
61	  finalFocusRef,
62	  children,
63	  messages,
64	  footer,
65	}: ZimmCartDrawerProps) => {
66	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_DRAWER_RECIPE, {});
67	  const title = itemCount === 0 ? 'YOUR BAG IS EMPTY' : `BAG • ${itemCount}`;
68	
69	  return (
70	    <ZimmDrawer
71	      isOpen={isOpen}
72	      onClose={onClose}
73	      size="xLarge"
74	      title={title}
75	      titleStyle="small"
76	      finalFocusRef={finalFocusRef}
77	    >
78	      <chakra.div __css={styles.messages}>{messages}</chakra.div>
79	      <chakra.div __css={styles.body}>
80	        {itemCount === 0 ? <chakra.p textStyle="body2">{EMPTY_BAG_PLACEHOLDER_TEXT}</chakra.p> : children}
81	      </chakra.div>
82	      <chakra.div __css={styles.footer}>{footer}</chakra.div>
83	    </ZimmDrawer>
84	  );
85	};

## Bottom line
Built and it works: `useCartMessages` now exists, all three cart toast messages fire through one real call, the copy is byte-exact, `tsc`/lint/full test suite are all clean, and I proved the tests actually catch a wrong value (not just tautologies) by breaking the hook on purpose and watching the right tests fail, then reverting. Two things Marcel should know about before this goes further: the plan file this step's own instructions pointed at doesn't live in this repo (see below — not a problem, just worth knowing), and step 4.6's own pass criteria (not this step's job) describes an integration with `ZimmCartDrawer` that this hook's design can't actually support as written — flagged at the bottom, not fixed, since it's outside this step's file manifest.

## Branch and plan-file location
- `git branch --show-current` → `feature/SFCC-11_cart`. Not `develop`/`main`. Confirmed before writing anything.
- `.runs/SFCC-11/plan.md` does not exist inside `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa` — it lives at `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-11/plan.md` (the sibling skills repo, alongside `HANDOFF.md` and `findings.md`). I found it there and read the corrected Step 4.3 section (lines 402–415) and `## 5.0 Verification standard` (lines 555–602) in full, plus `HANDOFF.md` and the relevant `findings.md` rows, before writing any code. Flagging the path mismatch factually in case it's not already known — it cost one dead end (a `find` over the whole filesystem that I killed once the sibling repo turned up the file directly) but nothing else.

## What I built
**`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.ts`** (new) — wraps the base `useToast` from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast` (confirmed real, read its source directly: destructures `{title, description, status, action, position='top-right', duration=5000, variant='subtle', isClosable=true}`, calls Chakra's own `toast(toastConfig)`). Does **not** create `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts`.

- One private `emitCartMessage(title, status)` closure is the sole place that calls `toast({title, status})` — line 93. The SFCC-404 marker sits directly above it:
  ```ts
  const emitCartMessage = (title: string, status: CartToastStatus): void => {
    // SFCC-404: this is the one real call to the underlying toast function. When SFCC-404's real
    // stacking/aggregation rework lands, this is the only line that changes.
    toast({ title, status });
  };
  ```
- Three named functions returned from the hook, each delegating to `emitCartMessage`:
  - `notifyAddedToWishlist(productName: string)` → `` `${productName} added to Wishlist` ``, status `success`.
  - `notifyAlreadyInWishlist()` → `'An item in your bag already exists in Wishlist'`, status `warning`.
  - `notifyMaxQuantityReached()` → `'An item in your bag has reached maximum quantity'`, status `warning`, **not** `error` — CAI-017's own wording says "error message," but I followed this build's own already-recorded resolution (`findings.md` finding #4: "Follow the design + AC (warning). Assumption stated: 'error' in CAI-017 means user-facing feedback, not the error severity tier") and the same reconciliation already documented in this codebase at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage/index.tsx` ("a caller may legitimately pass `variant=\"warning\"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word `error`"). Both `notifyAddedToWishlist`'s AC5 and `notifyAlreadyInWishlist`'s AC6 citations are pulled directly from plan.md's own step 4.4 pass-criteria text (lines 436–437), not invented.
- `useToast()`'s real return is implicit `any` — it resolves through `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts:185`'s catch-all `declare module '@salesforce/retail-react-app/*'`. I declared a narrow local type (`CartToastFn`, covering only `title`/`status` — the two fields this file actually sends) and cast to it with an inline comment explaining why, mirroring the exact pattern already used at `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:179-191`.

**`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.test.tsx`** (new, `.tsx` as directed) — mocks `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast` at the module boundary with a hoisted `vi.fn()`, the same mock this codebase already uses in three other places (`recommended-products/index.test.tsx`, `product-view/index.test.tsx`, `recentlyViewed/index.test.tsx`) specifically because the base `use-toast.js` ships JSX inside a `.js` file that Vitest's transform can't parse when pulled in transitively — I found this precedent before writing the test, not after, so I didn't rediscover the problem by trial and error. 6 tests: both wishlist-copy strings (including a second product name to prove it's a template, not a hardcoded fixture), the already-in-wishlist string, the max-quantity string, an explicit negative check that max-quantity never uses `status: 'error'`, and one test proving all three calls land on the same mocked function (no second, bypassing call site).

## Pass criteria — evidence, not assertion

**1. One emit site.** Ran the corrected grep exactly as written:
```
overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.ts:1:import { useToast } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast';
overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.ts:9: * another untyped base function), so the real `useToast()` return value is implicitly `any`.
overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.ts:72: * Wraps the **base** `useToast` (...) rather than a
overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.ts:88:  const toast = useToast() as CartToastFn;
overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.ts:93:    toast({ title, status });
```
Zero matches in `overrides/app/pages/cart` or `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**/zimmCart*` — confirming no second toast call exists anywhere else in cart UI. Literal line count is 5, not 1: two are prose inside doc comments, one is the import, one is acquiring the toast function (`useToast()`), and exactly **one** — line 93 — is a real dispatch call. The criterion's own text defines "emit site" as "the one real call to the underlying toast function," not a grep line-count target, so I'm reporting the real output plus this reading rather than silently rounding it down to "one line."

**2. Copy strings asserted verbatim.** All three strings, byte-compared against the task brief, are in the test with real `toHaveBeenCalledWith` assertions (not compared against the hook's own constants — that would be circular). Then I mutation-tested it for real: temporarily changed the interpolation order to `` `added to Wishlist ${productName}` `` and the max-quantity status to `'error'`, ran the suite, watched exactly the 4 dependent tests fail with the real wrong values printed (e.g. `- "title": "added to Wishlist Harlow Midi Dress"` / `+ "title": "Harlow Midi Dress added to Wishlist"`), while the 2 content-independent tests stayed green as designed, then reverted both lines and reran clean. This is the "prove, don't assert" standard applied to a small, cheap case — not something I'd redo for every trivial change, but worth doing once here since it's new logic.

**3. Storybook `play` — correctly not built.** Confirmed zero `.stories.tsx` files exist anywhere under `overrides/app/hooks/` today, and nothing renders cart-message UI yet (steps 4.4/4.6 don't exist). Deferred as instructed, not worked around.

**4. SFCC-404 marker present.** Read the file back after finishing (not assumed from memory) — confirmed at line 91-92, quoted above.

## Standard gates — before/after
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean, exit 0. Ran twice (before and after an eslint auto-fix pass).
- `npm run lint` on the two files — **first run failed with 14 prettier errors** (bracket-spacing: I wrote `{result}`/`{title, status}` instead of this repo's configured `{ result }`/`{ title, status }` — `.prettierrc`'s `bracketSpacing: true`). Ran `eslint --fix`, all 14 auto-fixed, re-ran lint clean (exit 0), re-ran `tsc` clean again, re-ran the test file — still 6/6 passing after the formatting fix. Reporting this rather than hiding it since it's a real gate that failed once before passing.
- `npm run test -- --run` (full suite) — **119 files / 1652 tests, all passed.** `git status --porcelain` confirms only the two new files exist in the working tree (nothing else staged, modified, or touched), so the pre-change baseline is arithmetically 118 files / 1646 tests — this is a purely additive change with nothing else touched, so re-running the unchanged baseline separately would just be re-proving something that can't have moved. `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` (the hard styling gate) is in that green run: 6/6, unaffected — expected, since this hook has zero styling.
- `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` — ran for completeness. Its own scope comment (`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs:10`) confirms it only scans `overrides/app/components/**` and `overrides/app/theme/components/**` — `overrides/app/hooks/` is outside its scan root entirely, same as the prior two hook-only steps (4.1/4.2). It found 9 unacknowledged pre-existing violations elsewhere in the codebase (none in files I touched, none newly introduced).

## What I did not touch
`git status --porcelain` shows exactly:
```
?? overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.test.tsx
?? overrides/app/hooks/useCartMessages.ts
```
No `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` created. No `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx`, no `ZimmCartItemActions`, no story. Nothing staged, nothing committed.

## Unverified gaps (mine)
- I have not proven this renders correctly in a live browser/real `ChakraProvider` — the test mocks the base `useToast` entirely, matching this codebase's own established reason for doing so (JSX-in-`.js` parse failure under Vitest) and matching pass-criterion 3's own explicit deferral. The base hook's default handling of the fields I omit (`description`, `action`, `position`, `duration`, `variant`, `isClosable`) is verified by reading its source directly (all have safe defaults or are guarded), not by running it live.
- The three function names (`notifyAddedToWishlist`, `notifyAlreadyInWishlist`, `notifyMaxQuantityReached`) are my own naming choice — the task specified behaviour and copy, not exact names. Whatever calls this hook in step 4.4/4.6 needs to match these; I have no way to verify that fit yet since neither exists.

## What Marcel is missing
`ZimmCartDrawer`'s own `messages` prop (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx:27`) is explicitly documented as "Reserved slot for **SFCC-404's** message-aggregation system" — but plan.md's own Step 4.6 pass criterion 5 (not built, not this step's job) says "`messages` slot renders whatever `useCartMessages` **currently holds**." Those two can't both be right: a Chakra toast (what this step was explicitly told to build) is fire-and-forget through its own independent portal — it has no "current value" to render into a slot, and the slot it would need to render into is already spoken for by a different, later ticket. Whoever scopes step 4.6 will hit this seam directly — worth resolving (either the slot isn't for the interim toast at all, or `useCartMessages` needs a second, state-based shape) before that step is dispatched, not discovered mid-build.
